The test scene is a 1.2gb 3ds Max file of a nine unit mid rise residential with full site landscaping, PBR interior sets in six units, and a Corona sky at 6:15pm. We rendered the same shot on all four cards at 4k with a fixed sample budget

RTX 5090 was the fastest card in every test. On the Corona shot it turned the reference frame in 11 minutes 40 seconds with the built in denoiser. V-Ray GPU came in at 8 minutes 20. Unreal path tracing hit clean convergence in 2 minutes 15 per frame at 4k. Chaos Vantage ran the walkthrough at 44 fps at 4k with DLSS 4 quality

RTX 4090 On the same Corona shot it turned the frame in 15 minutes 40 seconds, which is 34 percent slower than the 5090 in wall clock time. V-Ray came in at 11 minutes 30. Unreal path tracing was 3 minutes flat per frame. Chaos Vantage held 32 fps at 4k

RTX Pro 6000 is the workstation card. It has 96gb of VRAM. For our test scene it was fractionally slower than the 5090 on Corona because it runs at a lower clock, but it never got close to a VRAM ceiling, and it can hold multiple scenes in memory at once for interactive review
RTX 5080 16gb of VRAM. Our test scene pushed VRAM usage to 14.2gb in V-Ray GPU, which is uncomfortably close to the ceiling

Corona and V-Ray both scale nearly linearly across two GPUs of the same class. Two 4090s in a single machine beat a single 5090 on total render time and cost about the same. Unreal path tracing scales less well because of the way it batches frames. Chaos Vantage does not use the second GPU meaningfully in real time playback

If you are building a new primary workstation and money is not the driver, RTX 5090 with 1200 watt PSU and generous cooling. If you are adding a render node or building for value, RTX 4090 at whatever discount you can find. If you work on masterplan scale scenes, RTX Pro 6000
